rawFindings.title: Destructuring variable declarations are incorrectly reported with an undefined name
rawFindings.explanation: This guard no longer excludes non-Identifier declarator patterns. For destructuring declarations, `node.id.name` is undefined, so a named function initializer is treated as a mismatch even though there is no single variable name for this rule to compare.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the `node.id.type !== "Identifier"` check in this early return before reading `node.id.name`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With the default rule options and `parserOptions.ecmaVersion: 6`, linting `var {a} = function foo() {};` reports `Function name 'foo' should match variable name 'undefined'` instead of producing no `func-name-matching` report.

rawFindings.title: Destructuring assignments can crash the rule
rawFindings.explanation: The early return no longer filters assignment left-hand sides to Identifier or MemberExpression. For an ArrayPattern/ObjectPattern left-hand side, `name` becomes undefined and is passed to `isIdentifier`, which expects a string and can throw while linting valid ES6 destructuring syntax.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the left-hand-side type check, e.g. return unless `node.left.type` is `Identifier` or `MemberExpression`, before computing `name`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With the default rule options and `parserOptions.ecmaVersion: 6`, linting `[a] = function foo() {};` reaches `isIdentifier(undefined, ecmaVersion)` and throws instead of skipping the destructuring assignment.
